label: Bashkir horse

names.text: Alternate names as given in the research input. The fetched article text did not list them, so the page does not confirm them; 'Bashkir horse' is the article title.

about.text: A horse of Bashkortostan in Russia, bred mainly there with the main breeding centre in Ufa. Its mares are good milk producers, and most of the milk becomes kumis, a national activity of the Bashkir people.

sources.text: Article text: mainly raised in Bashkortostan, main breeding centre in Ufa; most of the milk becomes kumis, 'a national activity of the Bashkiri people'.
Article text: 'The origins of the Bashkir horse are not known.' Breeding centres were established in 1845. No formation year range is given, so none is recorded.
Article text: '2003: 94,470 horses reported.' The article does not say whether this is the breed alone; recorded as the breed's population as the article gives it.
Article text: 'Early 2011: almost 137,000.' The article's wording is approximate; 137,000 is the rounded figure. Same caveat on whether it is the breed alone.

links.name: FAO breed description (Bashkir), as quoted in search results

sources.text: Wikipedia gives an average of 1500 kg per year, and in another passage 2100 kg over a lactation of 240 days; the best mares reach 2700 kg. The FAO breed description (seen only as a WebSearch snippet, not fetched in full) gives an average of 1500 kg of marketable milk and 2700 kg for the best mares over 7 to 8 months of lactation. The two sources differ, so the range runs from 1500 to 2100 kg. Year and place of recording are not given. The best-mare figure of 2700 kg is kept in the text, not the range.
Article text: mares are abundant milk producers and most of the milk becomes kumis. The article names no other use.
Article text: 'DAD-IS (2022): unknown'. It also gives FAO (2007) as 'not at risk' with a figure of 98. Taken as the article reports it; not checked against DAD-IS itself.

facts.v: Its economic value was recognised in the 19th century, and breeding centres were established in 1845.

sources.text: Article text: economic value recognised in the 19th century; breeding centres established in 1845.

facts.v: Bashkortostan ranks third among Russian federal subjects for horse population, behind Altai Krai and the Sakha Republic.

sources.text: Article text ranks Bashkortostan third for horse population among Russian federal subjects. No year given.

gaps: Milk composition, the lactation curve and the place and year of the yield figures were not found. The FAO description was seen only in a search snippet; its full text could not be read because the PDF did not come back as text. Breed-only population is not confirmed, since the article's figures may cover all horses in the region.
